title: Περιστερὰ καὶ κορώνη
part: The Dove and the Crow (Chambry 302 · Perry 202)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 302 (= Perry 202). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Περιστερὰ ἔν τινι περιστεροτροφείῳ τρεφομένη ἐπὶ πολυτεκνίᾳ ἐφρυάττετο.
sentences.tr: Peristera en tini peristerotropheiōi trephomenē epi polytekniāi ephryatteto.
sentences.l: A dove, being kept in a dovecote, gave herself airs over her many young.
sentences.n: φρυάττομαι is properly of a horse snorting and tossing its head, and so of a creature giving itself airs; ἐπί with the dative names the ground of the display. πολυτεκνία is the having of many children — a thing counted a blessing among men, which is why the crow's answer stings.

sentences.t: Κορώνη δὲ ἀκούσασα αὐτῆς τῶν λόγων ἔφη· « Ἀλλ’, ὦ αὕτη, πέπαυσο ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἀλαζονευομένη· ὅσῳ γὰρ ἂν πλέονα τέκνα σχῇς, τοσούτῳ περισσοτέρας δουλείας στενάξεις. »
sentences.tr: Korōnē de akousasa autēs tōn logōn ephē· « All’, ō hautē, pepauso epi toutōi alazoneuomenē· hosōi gar an pleona tekna schēis, tosoutōi perissoteras douleias stenaxeis. »
sentences.l: But a crow, having heard her words, said: « But you there, have done with boasting over this; for by how much the more children you get, by so much the more slavery will you groan over. »
sentences.i: But a crow heard her talk and said: « You there — have done with boasting of that; the more young you get, the more slavery you will have to groan over. »
sentences.n: πέπαυσο is a perfect imperative, 'have done once and for all', a stronger stop than the present would give. ὦ αὕτη is the blunt way of hailing a woman, roughly 'you there' — the masculine ὦ οὗτος stands at fable 160. ὅσῳ … τοσούτῳ are datives of measure of difference, 'by as much … by so much'. The crow's point is that the young in a dovecote are bred for the keeper: every chick is one more life owned by another. περισσοτέρας δουλείας may be read as accusative plural after στενάξεις or as genitive singular; the sense is not affected.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν οἰκετῶν δυστυχέστατοί εἰσιν ὅσοι ἐν τῇ δουλείᾳ τεκνοποιοῦσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn oiketōn dystychestatoi eisin hosoi en tēi douleiāi teknopoiousin.
sentences.l: So too, among household slaves, the most unfortunate are those who have children in slavery.
sentences.n: A child born to a slave belonged to the master, not to the parents, so the slave who has children has only enlarged another man's property — the crow's dovecote exactly. The same shape of moral stands at fable 282, also drawn from οἰκέται.
